title: Restriction Digest
description: DNA digestion, fragment lengths, and absorbance measurements

blocks.text:
Write a summary of the restriction digest experiment, its objectives, and conclusions between one paragraph and one page in length.

The restriction digest experiment is to use restriction enzymes to perform specific cuts at
desired short DNA fragments (restriction sites) of around 6-8 base pairs long. The
enzymes will apply 2 cuts one near both ends of the restriction site. The process results
in DNA fragments of various sizes which can be quantitatively predicted by analyzing a
map of the original DNA as well as the known locations where the selected enzyme is
expected to cut.
In this experiment, our goal was to perform restriction digest procedures with necessary
controls in order to verify that our experiment proceeded as expected. We verified the
action of the applied restriction enzymes by running/inspecting DNA fragments on a gel,
to observe whether the lengths of the resulting DNA fragments were as expected. We
found that the fragment lengths aligned with our expectations from restriction map
analysis, demonstrating successfully the function of restriction digests.
---

sections.title: Problem 2: Sticky Ends in Restriction Digests

blocks.text:
Which of the three restriction enzymes we used in lab result in 3′ overhangs? Which result in 5′ overhangs?

- **5′ overhangs**: EcoRI, HindIII  
- **3′ overhang**: KpnI
-

Using this map: http://bi1x.caltech.edu/2023/handouts/neb_lambda_restriction_sites.pdf

### a) Single digestion with HindIII:
- 9416 bp, 23130 bp, 2322 bp, 564 bp, 2027 bp, 2682 bp

### b) Single digestion with EcoRI:
- 5643 bp, 21226 bp, 4887 bp, 6421 bp, 5804 bp, 3530 bp

### c) Double digestion with HindIII and EcoRI:
- 2027 bp, 1375 bp, 4268 bp, 5148 bp, 564 bp, 1709 bp, 4963 bp, 831 bp, 1904 bp, 3530 bp, 21226 bp

Approximated lengths of fragments observed in the double digest lane:

- more than 10k bp  
- 5–6k bp  
- 4 kb  
- 3 kb  
- 2 kb  
- 1.5 kb  
- <1 kb  

The number of DNA bands that we were able to discern is less than expected, we think
that it is because some of the expected fragment lengths were very similar to each other,
so the representative bands may have smeared together due to imperfections on the gel
protocol. But the size of the bands mostly aligned with the sizes of fragments we
expected, suggesting that the digestion procedure was successful.

Make a plot of OD starch/iodine concentration from your serial dilution-absorbance measurements. Your concentration should be in units of the most concentrated solution. For example, a 100× dilution has a concentration of 0.01.

![Absorbance Plot](/bi1x/images/lab-1-02124c0e.jpg)

**Does the plot make sense?**  
The plot makes sense as the iodine conc mostly follows a directly proportional
relationship with starch. This result is expected as there should be a greater absorbance
from the starch complex when there is a greater iodine conc.

sections.title: Problem 6: Safety Always on the Mind

blocks.text:
List three hazards in the Bi 1x lab and how you will protect yourself from them:

Potential hazardous materials (ex: chemical compounds that could irritate the
skin) - use gloves when handling chemical compounds to prevent direct contact
with the skin.
Potential biological contamination (ex: Ecoli on my clothes) - wear the provided
lab coats whenever in the lab, and follow any TA/instructor directions on how to
handle the materials.
Tripping/falling in the lab, potentially knocking over sensitive/large/delicate devices
and items - wear closed-toed shoes whenever in the lab, and move around
carefully
